title: The odd prayer
hookLine: the odd-numbered night prayer, strongly stressed, wajib in the Hanafi school

lines: FAST, PRAY IN THE MORNING, PRAY WITR.
A PRAYER AT THE EDGE OF SLEEP.
cards: Abu Hurayrah once said his close friend had advised him to keep three things until he died. His close friend was the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him.

The three: fasting three days every month, praying two units in the late morning, and praying witr before going to sleep. Sahih al-Bukhari keeps the list, at number 1178. Two of those are about daylight.
The last is about the moment just before you turn out the light, the phone on the charger, the day nearly done.

teach.h: WITR: AN ODD NUMBER OF UNITS.
teach.b: Witr means odd, as in an odd number. It's the prayer with an odd count of units that closes the night's praying: one, or three, or more, so long as the total comes out odd. Why odd?

teach.h: ALLAH IS WITR AND LOVES WITR.
teach.b: In Sahih al-Bukhari, number 6410, the Prophet ﷺ says that Allah is witr, and loves witr. The same word that names this prayer is used of God: single, one, not paired.
Some teachers read ending the night on an odd number as a small sign of that oneness, the tawhid this path has already met, written into the shape of a prayer. When is it prayed?
Any time after the night prayer, isha, until dawn. In Sahih al-Bukhari, number 998, he says: make witr the last of your prayer at night. And Sahih Muslim, number 755, gives a practical choice.

teach.h: LAST OF THE NIGHT, OR BEFORE SLEEP.
teach.b: Whoever fears they won't wake in the last part of the night should pray witr before sleeping. Whoever expects to wake can pray it at the end, because prayer at the end of the night is witnessed.
That's Abu Hurayrah's choice in the hook: witr before sleep, so it's never lost. How binding is it? Here the schools differ, and they say so openly.
The Hanafi school holds witr to be wajib, necessary, a step below the obligatory prayers but not to be dropped.

teach.h: WAJIB FOR HANAFIS, STRONGLY STRESSED FOR OTHERS.
teach.b: The other Sunni schools hold it to be a strongly stressed sunnah, not obligatory.

teach.h: MAKE WITR THE LAST OF YOUR PRAYER.
teach.b: Either way, it's the prayer the day ends on.

how: Muslims pray witr after the night prayer and before dawn, as one, three or more units so the total is odd; some pray it before sleep and some at the end of the night, and the Hanafi school counts it as wajib while the other Sunni schools treat it as a strongly stressed sunnah.

games.q: you want to pray witr, but you're not sure you'll wake before dawn. what does the hadith in Muslim 755 suggest?
games.why: whoever fears not waking prays witr at the start of the night; whoever expects to wake can pray it at the end.

practice: Let the day slow down. If you pray, you can settle now on praying witr tonight before sleep, even a single unit, so the night ends on it; if you don't, count your breaths slowly, one, two, three, and stop on an odd number.
One last breath, alone and unpaired, then rest in what's left of the quiet.

wordCard.voice: Witr. Odd. The prayer with an odd number of units that ends the night, wajib for the Hanafi school and strongly stressed for the other Sunni schools. Today's word.
